# Commercial Term Loan Agreement

*Synthetic document for pipeline validation. No real parties, figures, or events.*

### 1. Parties

This Commercial Term Loan Agreement ("Agreement") is entered into between Meridian Manufacturing LLC,
a limited liability company ("Borrower"), and Highland Capital Bank, N.A. ("Lender").

### 2. Loan Amount

2.1 The Lender agrees to extend a term loan to the Borrower in the principal amount of $4,200,000
(the "Loan").

### 3. Interest Rate

3.1 The Loan shall bear interest at a fixed rate of 7.25% per annum, calculated on the outstanding
principal balance, payable monthly in arrears.

### 4. Maturity

4.1 The Loan shall mature 84 months from the date of this Agreement, at which point all outstanding
principal and accrued interest shall be due in full.

### 5. Financial Covenants

5.1 Borrower shall maintain a minimum Debt Service Coverage Ratio (DSCR) of 1.30x, tested quarterly
based on trailing twelve-month financials.

5.2 Borrower shall maintain a maximum Loan-to-Value (LTV) ratio of 82%, based on the most recent
appraisal of the Collateral.

5.3 Borrower shall maintain a maximum leverage ratio (Total Debt / EBITDA) of 3.2x, tested quarterly.

5.4 Borrower shall use commercially reasonable efforts to maintain adequate working capital reserves
throughout the term of this Agreement.

### 6. Collateral

6.1 As security for the Loan, Borrower grants Lender a first-priority lien on the manufacturing facility
located at 4400 Industrial Parkway, Austin, TX 78744, as more particularly described in Schedule A.

### 7. Reporting Obligations

7.1 Borrower shall deliver to Lender quarterly unaudited financial statements within 45 days of each
fiscal quarter end, and annual audited financial statements within 120 days of each fiscal year end.

### 8. Events of Default

8.1 Each of the following constitutes an Event of Default under this Agreement:
(a) failure to pay any principal or interest when due;
(b) breach of any financial covenant in Section 5;
(c) any material misrepresentation by Borrower;
(d) insolvency or bankruptcy filing by Borrower;
(e) a change of control of Borrower without Lender's prior written consent.

### 9. Prepayment

9.1 Borrower may prepay the Loan in whole or in part at any time upon 30 days' written notice, subject
to a prepayment premium of 2% of the amount prepaid if prepayment occurs within the first 24 months.

### 10. Governing Law

10.1 This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of
New York.

### 11. Schedule A — Collateral Description

11.1 Manufacturing facility, approximately 62,000 square feet, situated on a 4.1-acre parcel at
4400 Industrial Parkway, Austin, TX 78744, together with all fixtures and equipment affixed thereto.

risks.title: Excessive Loan‑to‑Value Ratio
risks.rationale: The covenant sets LTV at 82%, which exceeds the allowed maximum of 75% per policy, increasing loss severity in adverse scenarios.

evidence.quote: Maximum Loan-to-Value (LTV) Ratio (covenant): 82%

risks.mitigation: Renegotiate the LTV covenant, add supplemental collateral, or reduce the loan amount to bring LTV within policy limits.

risks.title: Missing Definition of Change of Control
risks.rationale: Clause 8.1 references a change of control event without defining the term, creating ambiguity and potential disputes over consent requirements.

evidence.quote: a change of control of Borrower without Lender's prior written consent

risks.mitigation: Request the borrower to insert a precise definition of "Change of Control" and outline the lender's consent process.

risks.title: Absent Principal Repayment Schedule
risks.rationale: The agreement specifies loan amount and maturity but does not detail periodic principal repayments, hindering cash‑flow planning and covenant monitoring.

evidence.quote: Loan Amount (value): $4,200,000

risks.mitigation: Obtain a detailed amortization schedule outlining payment dates and amounts.

risks.title: No Collateral Appraisal Provided
risks.rationale: While a first‑priority lien is granted (clause 6.1), the absence of an appraisal date/value prevents accurate valuation of the security.

evidence.quote: First‑priority lien on the manufacturing facility located at 4400 Industrial Parkway, Austin, TX 78744

risks.mitigation: Secure an independent appraisal of the manufacturing facility and attach the report to the loan file.

risks.title: Origination Fee Not Disclosed
risks.rationale: The agreement does not mention any origination fee, which may affect total loan cost and compliance with fee disclosure policies.
risks.mitigation: Confirm with the lender whether an origination fee applies and obtain written disclosure if so.

risks.title: Exact Calendar Maturity Date Unspecified
risks.rationale: Clause 4.1 provides a term of 84 months but does not state the specific maturity date, complicating schedule tracking.

evidence.quote: Maturity (date): 84 months from the date of this Agreement

risks.mitigation: Request the precise maturity date based on the agreement execution date.

executive_summary: The loan agreement for Meridian Manufacturing LLC presents several material risks: the LTV covenant of 82% exceeds the policy limit of 75%, and key terms such as the principal repayment schedule, collateral appraisal, origination fee, and a precise definition of Change of Control are absent, creating legal and operational uncertainty. These gaps, combined with the high‑risk LTV breach, elevate financial and compliance exposure. Immediate clarification and amendment of the missing provisions are required to mitigate potential defaults and regulatory concerns.
follow_up_actions: Obtain a formal collateral appraisal and document the valuation date and amount.
Negotiate a reduction of the LTV ratio or provide additional collateral to meet the 75% policy ceiling.
Request a detailed principal repayment schedule, including dates and amounts.
Add a clear definition of "Change of Control" and any associated consent requirements.
Confirm whether an origination fee applies and, if so, disclose its amount and terms.
Specify the exact calendar maturity date for the 84‑month term.
